title: Changing opportunities

blocks.heading: Changing opportunities
blocks.text: Women’s participation in jobs, public decisions and projects can expand through access reforms, skills and support arrangements. A new opportunity needs usable access. Participation percentages should identify the eligible group and distinguish attendance, completion and decision-making influence.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Access to jobs
blocks.text: Equal job access concerns fair opportunities to apply, gain relevant skills and be considered without gender discrimination. Selection rules, transport, caring duties and workplace treatment can affect actual access. A higher total number of jobs does not show who can obtain them.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Policies and implementation
blocks.text: Policies can set equality aims and change procedures, but need responsibilities, resources and monitoring. A rule’s adoption is an output; reduced barriers or wider influence are outcomes. Compare implementation evidence rather than assuming a policy announcement resolves inequality.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Targeted schemes
blocks.text: Women-oriented schemes can address a documented gap in finance, skills, services or participation. Targeting can improve access where the barrier is real, but eligibility, timing and decision rules can still exclude some intended participants.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Female-headed households
blocks.text: A female-headed household has a woman identified as its head under the definition used. It is not automatically poor or identical to other such households. Income, resources, care responsibilities and support need evidence rather than assumptions from the label.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: A practical access test
blocks.text: Describe this fictional programme: equal admission rules remain unchanged, but after timetable revision women’s attendance rises from 40% to 70% and completion from 30% to 55%. Attendance and completion both improve, by 30 and 25 percentage points, while formal rules are unchanged. Practical access changes therefore accompany gains beyond written admission equality.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect to traditional roles (6.1), education (7.3) and research (10.1). Use evidence about resources, voice and practical access. Fictional cases do not establish current law, service availability or a diagnosis about any individual.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
